Mathematics.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
Mathematics.abstract: The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we…

Mathematics.title: The Gopakumar--Vafa finiteness conjecture
Mathematics.abstract: The Gopakumar--Vafa conjecture predicts that the BPS invariants of a symplectic 6-manifold, defined in terms of the Gromov--Witten invariants, are integers and all but finitely many vanish in every homology class. The integrality part of this conjecture was proved earlier by Ionel and Parker. This article proves the finiteness part. The proof relies on a modification of Ionel and Parker's cluster formalism using results from geometric measure theory.

Mathematics.title: Hyperbolic Large Language Models
Mathematics.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success and demonstrated superior performance across various tasks, including natural language processing (NLP), weather forecasting, biological protein folding, text generation, and solving mathematical problems. However, many real-world data exhibit highly non-Euclidean latent hierarchical anatomy, such as protein networks, transportation networks, financial networks, brain networks, and linguistic structures or syntactic trees in natural languages. Effectively learning intrinsic semantic entailment and hierarchical relationships from these raw, unstructured input data using LLMs remains an underexplored area. Due to its effectiveness in modeling tree-like hierarchical structures, hyperbolic geometry—a non-Euclidean space—has rapidly gained popularity as an expressive latent representation space for complex data modeling across…

Mathematics.title: On a conjecture of Almgren: area-minimizing submanifolds with fractal singular sets
Mathematics.abstract: We construct area-minimizing submanifolds with fractal singular sets on compact Riemannian manifolds. Thus, we settle a conjecture of Almgren, and our answer is sharp dimension-wise. Furthermore, we can prescribe arbitrarily the strata in the Almgren stratification of the singular sets of our area-minimizing submanifolds, and our results hold in the category of integral currents, mod v currents and stable stationary varifolds.

Mathematics.title: An Introduction to Computational Fluctuating Hydrodynamics
Mathematics.abstract: This short article is an introduction to the theory of fluctuating hydrodynamics (FHD) and the formulation of numerical schemes for the resulting stochastic partial differential equations. The stochastic heat equation (SHE) is derived, and simple finite-volume schemes for its solution are outlined. Numerical results from a Python program (see the supplementary materials ( supplement.pdf [ 196KB])) are shown to be in good agreement with theoretical solutions of the SHE for equilibrium and nonequilibrium systems. Finally, a menagerie of other FHD equations is outlined and suggested instructional exercises are listed.

Mathematics.title: High-dimensional families of holomorphic curves and three-dimensional energy surfaces
Mathematics.abstract: Let $H: \mathbb{R}^4 \to \mathbb{R}$ be any smooth function. This article introduces some arguments for extracting dynamical information about the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ from high-dimensional families of closed holomorphic curves. We work in a very general setting, without imposing convexity or contact-type assumptions. For any compact regular level set $Y$, we prove that the Hamiltonian flow admits an infinite family of pairwise distinct, proper, compact invariant subsets whose union is dense in $Y$. This is a generalization of the Fish--Hofer theorem, which showed that $Y$ has at least one proper compact invariant subset. We then establish a global Le Calvez--Yoccoz property for almost every compact regular level set $Y$: any compact invariant subset containing all closed orbits is either equal to $Y$ or is not locally maximal. Next, we prove quantitative versions, in four…

Mathematics.title: Reconciling Discrete-Time Mixed Policies and Continuous-Time Relaxed Controls in Reinforcement Learning and Stochastic Control
Mathematics.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is currently one of the most prominent methods for optimizing dynamical systems, with breakthrough results across various fields. The framework is based on the concept of a Markov decision process (MDP), leading to a discrete-time optimal control problem. In the RL literature, such problems are typically formulated and solved using mixed policies, from which random actions are sampled at each time step. Recently, part of the optimal control community has begun investigating continuous-time versions of RL algorithms, replacing MDPs with continuous-time stochastic processes governed by relaxed controls and asserting a full analogy between the two formulations. In this work, we examine the limitations of this analogy and rigorously establish a connection between the two problems in the case where only the drift term of the continuous-time model is controlled.…

Mathematics.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
Mathematics.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as…

Mathematics.title: Landau Damping and Plasma Echoes
Mathematics.abstract: This review article provides an overview and the state of the art of the study of Landau damping and plasma echoes in the classical Vlasov–Poisson system near spatially homogeneous equilibria that describes the dynamics of a plasma confined on a torus or in the whole space. In particular, the article reproduces an analyticity framework developed for nonspecialists in [E. Grenier, T. T. Nguyen, and I. Rodnianski, SIAM J. Math. Anal., 54 (2022), pp. 940–953] that constructs plasma echo solutions consisting of infinitely many interacting elementary waves with arbitrarily high frequencies. The echo solutions allow a much larger class of data than those in analytic or Gevrey spaces studied by Mouhot and Villani, now including certain data with arbitrarily large Sobolev norms; nonetheless, these solutions do exhibit Landau damping in the large time.

Mathematics.title: The Huang–Yang conjecture for the low-density Fermi gas
Mathematics.abstract: Our work establishes a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy of a dilute gas of spin $1/2$ 1 / 2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, validating a formula predicted by Huang and Yang in 1957. The formula is universal in the sense that it holds for a large class of interaction potentials and depends on those only via their scattering length. We have recently proved an upper bound on the ground state energy of the desired form, and the present work completes the program by proving the matching lower bound.

Mathematics.title: Optimization Problems with Nonconvexities Involving the Euclidean Norm: Challenges, Progress, and Opportunities
Mathematics.abstract: The field of global optimization has advanced significantly over the past three decades, yet the solution to global optimality of even small instances of many optimization problems with nonconvexities involving the Euclidean norm remains beyond the reach of modern global optimization methods. These problems include numerous well-known and high-impact open research questions from a diverse collection of both fundamental and applied fields of science and engineering. In this review, we survey applications in which these problems arise, describe sources of computational intractability, summarize existing solution methods, and identify promising research directions for future work. We also introduce EuclidLib, a library of instances of optimization problems of this type, to aid in performance benchmarking and algorithm development. The solution to global optimality of all problems in…

Mathematics.title: Effective gaps between singular values of non-stationary matrix products subject to non-degenerate noise
Mathematics.abstract: We study the singular values and Lyapunov exponents of non-stationary random matrix products subject to small, absolutely continuous, additive noise. Consider a fixed sequence of matrices of bounded norm. Independently perturb the matrices by additive noise distributed according to Lebesgue measure on matrices with norm less than $\epsilon $ ϵ . Then the gaps between the logarithms of the singular values of the random product of $n$ n of these matrices are all of order at least $\epsilon ^{2}n$ ϵ 2 n , both in expectation; and almost surely for large $n$ n . To prove this, we develop recent work of Gorodetski and Kleptsyn [26]. That paper gives a very flexible method, based on relative entropy, for showing that a non-stationary product of matrices in $\operatorname{SL}(d,\mathbb{R})$ SL ( d , R ) has a strictly positive Lyapunov exponent. Physics.title: Higgsino dark matter interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV nuclear-recoil event
Physics.abstract: We propose Higgsino dark matter as a potential interpretation of the $248~\mathrm{keV}$ nuclear-recoil event of interest reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment. LZ studied several rare background processes and detector effects in detail, but did not identify any as a likely explanation of the event. A nearly pure Higgsino naturally realizes inelastic dark matter through the off-diagonal $Z$ coupling of two nearly degenerate neutral Majorana states separated by a mass splitting $δ$. The same electroweak interaction fixes the inelastic Higgsino-nucleon scattering cross section, rather than leaving it as a free parameter. We show that the predicted Higgsino inelastic scattering cross section approaches the published LZ two-sided 90% confidence interval for a Higgsino mass $m_{\widetilde H}\sim1~\mathrm{TeV}$ and a mass splitting $δ\sim350~\mathrm{keV}$.

Physics.title: Any-light-particle searches with ALPSII: First science results
Physics.abstract: The light-shining-through-a-wall experiment ALPS II at DESY in Hamburg searched for axions and similar lightweight particles in its first science campaign from February to May 2024. No evidence for the existence of such particles was found. For pseudoscalar bosons like the axion, with masses below about 0.1 meV, we achieved a limit for the di-photon coupling strength of 1.5e-9 1/GeV at a 95% confidence level. This is more than a factor of 20 improvement compared to all previous similar experiments. We also provide limits on photon interactions for scalar, vector and tensor bosons. An achievement of this first science campaign is the demonstration of stable operation and robust calibration of the complex experiment. Currently, the optical system of ALPS II is being upgraded aiming for another two orders of magnitude sensitivity increase.

Physics.title: Bouncing singularities in Schwarzschild geometry: A geometric origin of the quasinormal mode convergence region
Physics.abstract: We show analytically that the convergence of the QNM expansion of the retarded Green's function of the Schwarzschild spacetime is set by a singularity in the complex time plane. The singularity has a simple geometric origin: it is an example of a `bouncing singularity' in the language of AdS/CFT literature, caused by a null geodesic which bounces from the black hole singularity. Our work explains why the QNM convergence region at real times is bounded by null ray which scatters from the gravitational potential at a seemingly unremarkable point ($r_* = 0$ in the conventions of previous work) -- this ray is the same distance from the origin as the bouncing singularity in the relevant complex plane. The same set of singularities are responsible for an annular region of convergence for the Matsubara mode sum which describes the early time behaviour of the Schwarzschild Green's function for…

Physics.title: Anomaly to resource: The Mpemba effect in quantum thermometry
Physics.abstract: Quantum thermometry provides a key capability for nanoscale devices and quantum technologies, but most existing strategies rely on probes initialized near equilibrium. This equilibrium paradigm imposes intrinsic limitations: sensitivity is tied to long-time thermalization and often cannot be improved in fast, noisy, or nonstationary settings. In contrast, the \textit{Mpemba effect}, the counterintuitive phenomenon where hotter states relax faster than colder ones, has mostly been viewed as a thermodynamic anomaly. Here, we bridge this gap by proving that Mpemba-type inversions generically yield a finite-time enhancement of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for temperature estimation, thereby converting an anomalous relaxation effect into a concrete metrological resource. Through explicit analyses of two-level and $Λ$-level probes coupled to bosonic baths, we show that nonequilibrium…

Physics.title: Conserved quantities enable the quantum Mpemba effect in weakly open systems
Physics.abstract: Observation of the quantum Mpemba effect has spurred much interest in its enabling conditions and its relation to the classical counterpart. Here, we consider weakly open many-body quantum systems initialized in different thermal states and examine when the initially farther state relaxes to the (non-equilibrium) steady state faster. We claim that the number of conserved quantities in the unitary part plays a crucial role: the Mpemba effect is possible only when the Hamiltonian commutes with other extensive operators or is integrable. The reason lies in the dynamical evolution happening in spaces of different dimensions. When energy is the only approximately conserved quantity, dissipation pushes the dynamics within a single-parameter manifold of different thermal states. In contrast, for Hamiltonians with several conserved quantities, the dynamics drift in the multi-dimensional space…

Physics.title: Scalable generation of macroscopic Fock states exceeding 10,000 photons
Physics.abstract: The scalable preparation of bosonic quantum states with macroscopic excitations poses a fundamental challenge in quantum technologies, limited by control complexity and photon-loss rates that severely constrain prior theoretical and experimental efforts to merely dozens of excitations per mode. Here, based on the duality of the quantum state evolution in Fock state space and the optical wave-function propagation in a waveguide array, we introduce a Kerr-engineered multi-lens protocol in a single bosonic mode to deterministically generate Fock states exceeding $10,000$ photons. By optimizing phase and displacement operations across lens groups, our approach compensates for non-paraxial aberrations, achieving fidelities above $73\%$ in numerical simulations for photon numbers up to $N=100,000$. Counterintuitively, the protocol's execution time scales as $N^{-1/2}$ with the target photon…

Physics.title: Exorcising ghosts with gravitational waves
Physics.abstract: General Relativity (GR) is an effective field theory valid in the infrared regime. Quadratic curvature extensions intended to probe ultraviolet physics generically propagate a massive spin-$2$ ghost and are therefore non-unitary. One route to remove ghost is by enlarging the geometric sector (torsion, non-metricity). We investigate the infrared phenomenology of both the standard (ghostful) and ghost-free fourth-order gravity theories by computing Gravitational Wave (GW) emission and confronting the results with observations such as the orbital-period decay of quasi-stable binaries such as PSR B1913+16 and PSR J1738+0333 and the chirp-mass evolution of GW170817. In the ghostful theory, besides the theoretical inconsistency due to non-unitarity, there are also phenomenological problems: the massless spin-$2$ GW flux cancels the combined GW fluxes of the massive spin-$2$ ghost and massive…

Physics.title: Sound propagation in striped supersolid gases at zero temperature
Physics.abstract: The role of dimensionality in the identification of sound modes in many-body systems characterized by the spontaneous breaking of translational symmetry is a topic of high interdisciplinary interest in both classical and quantum systems. The emergence of stripes in superfluids is a particularly interesting example where the dimensionality of the system differs from the one of the crystal phase. Here we present a unified hydrodynamic approach for the sound propagation in the stripe phase realized in ultracold dipolar and spin-orbit-coupled Bose gases at zero temperature. Despite the deep difference of the two platforms at a microscopic level, a similar hydrodynamic description can be formulated at a macroscopic level. Physics.title: Gate-based readout and cooling of neutral atoms
Physics.abstract: Neutral atom arrays have seen tremendous progress in quantum simulation, quantum metrology, and fault-tolerant quantum computing. However, hardware constraints such as atom loss and heating remain significant challenges. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive ancilla-based toolbox for optical tweezer experiments that utilizes high-fidelity Rydberg entangling gates and ancilla atoms to mitigate these physical limitations. First, we demonstrate repeated ancilla-based atom readout, achieving improved detection fidelity over multiple rounds with minimal perturbation to data atoms. Second, leveraging the quantized motional states in tweezer-trapped strontium atoms, we transduce quantum information from the electronic to the motional manifold. This enables us to perform mid-circuit ancilla-based atom loss detection in a coherence-preserving fashion. Finally, we demonstrate algorithmic…

Physics.title: S = 1 pyrochlore magnets with competing anisotropies: A tale of two Coulomb phases, Z 2 flux confinement, and XY-like transitions
Physics.abstract: We argue that the low-temperature physics of $S=1$ pyrochlore magnets with a predominantly Ising-like easy-axis exchange coupling $J$ that favors the local tetrahedral body diagonals, and a comparably large easy-plane single-ion anisotropy $Δ=J + μ$ ($|μ| \ll J$) that favors the plane perpendicular to these local axes will exhibit interesting new phenomena due to the competition between $J$ and $Δ$. In the $T/J \rightarrow 0$ limit, we find three low temperature phases as a function of $μ/T$: a short-range correlated paramagnetic phase, and two topologically-distinct Coulomb liquids separated by a $Z_2$ flux confinement transition. Both Coulomb liquids are described at long-wavelengths by a fluctuating divergence-free polarization field and have characteristic pinch-point singularities in their structure factor. In one Coulomb phase, the flux of this polarization field is confined to…

Physics.title: Nuclear charge radius of 9 Be from muonic atom spectroscopy using a microcalorimeter
Physics.abstract: The $2p\to1s$ transition energy in muonic $^9$Be was measured using a metallic magnetic calorimeter, resulting in $E_{2p\to 1s}=33\,391.48(34)\,$eV. The result is 30 times more precise than the previous best measurement and enables the extraction of the corresponding nuclear charge radius $r_c($$^9$Be$)=2.5506(51)\,$fm. It is $2.4$ times more precise than the commonly used value based on electron scattering and differs from it by $2.3$ times the combined uncertainties. This measurement represents the first determination of a nuclear charge radius using muonic x-ray spectroscopy with microcalorimeters.

Physics.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
Physics.abstract: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron's position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today. This review traces its development into a spectrum of mathematical formulations -- known as uncertainty relations -- and explores their interconnections and wide-ranging applications. We highlight its central role in quantum metrology, where it underpins strategies for extracting information from quantum systems with ever-increasing precision, and its links to multiparameter estimation and squeezed states. This review, dedicated to the centenary of the uncertainty principle, reflects on how it has deepened…

Physics.title: Finite-bias Coulomb blockade thermometry
Physics.abstract: Coulomb blockade thermometers (CBTs) are versatile and, in principle, primary thermometers operating down to the micro-Kelvin range but bias heating spoils the thermometry and the primary mode. Here, we introduce a method to extract the CBT electron temperature in the presence of heat created by an arbitrary bias voltage, and without assumptions on the heat flow mechanisms. The charging energy is extracted with high precision and without any other knowledge, thus making true primary thermometry possible. The experiment also reveals a subtle dependence of the charging energy on phonon temperature below 100 mK likely due to the amorphous AlO$_x$ tunnel junctions.

Physics.title: Defect assignment of the clock site in 229 Th:CaF 2
Physics.abstract: The performance of solid-state $^{229}\text{Th}$ nuclear clocks depends sensitively on the microscopic environment of the thorium nucleus in the host crystal. Here we reassess the dominant quadrupole-split thorium site in $^{229}\text{Th:CaF}_2$, which has been assigned to a thorium dimer in recent spectroscopic work. Thermodynamic estimates, density functional theory calculations, and electric-field-gradient comparisons instead favor an isolated $\text{Th}^{4+}$ substitution on a $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ site charge-compensated by two nearby fluorine interstitials in a relaxed $90^\circ$ motif. The same calculation identifies a higher-energy mixed-shell interstitial motif as a plausible minor site. The clock-active quadrupole-split site is therefore controlled by local fluoride compensation rather than unavoidable thorium aggregation. This defect assignment also has implications for…

Physics.title: 5/9-magnetization plateau and possible spin supersolidity in ${\rm YCu_3(OD)_7xBr_{2+x}}$ under magnetic fields up to 120 T
Physics.abstract: We performed high-precision magnetization measurements up to 120~T on three compositions of the newly discovered kagome antiferromagnet YCu$_3$(OD)$_{7-x}$Br$_{2+x}$ (YCOB), revealing a previously unobserved 5/9 fractional magnetization plateau. All YCOB samples with different Br$^-$ concentrations exhibit nearly identical magnetization curves below 60~T, whereas the 5/9 plateau appears at markedly different fields in the ultrahigh-field regime. By modeling the experimental data using tensor-network calculations, we derive the effective spin Hamiltonians for the YCOB family with three spatially anisotropic Heisenberg couplings (the 3$J$-type model), which quantitatively reproduces the measured magnetization processes and captures the composition-dependent evolution of the 5/9 plateau. Furthermore, our theoretical analysis suggests the emergence of a spin supersolid phase in the field…

Earth and space.title: (LRDs) 2 : The Low-ReDshift Little Red Dots Survey. II. DESI DR1 Sample
Earth and space.abstract: JWST has revealed a substantial population of “Little Red Dots” (LRDs) at z > 4, challenging conventional active galactic muclei (AGN) frameworks. However, the low-redshift regime remains largely unexplored. In the second paper of the (LRDs) 2 series, we present a systematic selection from DESI DR1 and identify 27 LRDs at z = 0.2–0.9, yielding a number density lower limit of 7.5 × 10 −10 cMpc −3 . We conducted near-IR spectroscopic follow-up observations for 21 of them, revealing their full spectral energy distribution (SED) shapes and emission lines. These low- z LRDs share the hallmark properties of their high- z counterparts: compact morphology, V-shaped UV-optical continua, broad Balmer emission with extreme decrements (median H α /H β ∼ 15), frequent Balmer absorption (70%), and blackbody-like optical-to-near-IR continua. Earth and space.title: Banana Split: Improved Cosmological Constraints with Two Light-curve-shape and Color Populations Using Union3.1+UNITY1.8
Earth and space.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) have been used to provide key constraints on the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy. They are generally standardized under the assumption that they belong to a single population, with luminosities standardized in a continuous (roughly linear) fashion using the observed light-curve timescale. We update the Union3+UNITY1.5 supernova (SN) cosmology analysis in light of increasing evidence for at least two core populations of SNe Ia and apply this “UNITY1.8” model to the updated “Union3.1” compilation. In addition to finding evidence for two different light-curve-shape ( x 1 ) distributions, we also find that the color distributions are different, that the light-curve-shape/magnitude standardization relations are different, and that these populations have different distributions across host-galaxy stellar mass and redshift. Earth and space.title: Eight New Ultramassive Black Hole Masses Confirm Best Correlation with Galaxy Core Sizes
Earth and space.abstract: We analyze black hole (BH) scaling relations at the high-mass end, focusing in particular on the regime of ultramassive black holes, M BH > 10 10 M ⊙ (UMBHs). Building on the new dynamical BH mass measurements presented in our companion paper for a sample of 16 brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs), including eight newly identified UMBHs based on triaxial Schwarzschild models, we investigate the implications of these measurements for BH scaling relations. This first sample of triaxial BH mass determinations increases the number of known UMBHs by a factor of 2 and dramatically increases the constraints for BH mass scaling relations at the high-mass end. We find that BCGs are outliers in the canonical M BH ∝ σ 4−5 relation, while the size of their depleted cores—the central light-deficient region—offers a tighter correlation with M BH with a scatter of 0.22 dex in this mass regime,…

Earth and space.title: diffhydro : Inverse Multiphysics Modeling and Embedded Machine Learning in Astrophysical Flows
Earth and space.abstract: We present the extension of the differentiable hydrodynamics code, diffhydro , enabling scalable partial differential equation-constrained inference and integrated hybrid physics–machine learning (ML) models for a wide range of astrophysical applications. New physics additions include radiative heating/cooling, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck–driven turbulence, and self-gravity via multigrid Poisson. We demonstrate good agreement with the Athena++ code on standard validation tests like Sedov–Taylor, Kelvin–Helmholtz, and driven/decaying turbulence. We further introduce a solver-in-the-loop neural corrector that reduces coarse-grid errors during time integration while preserving stability. The addition of custom adjoints facilitates efficient end-to-end gradients and multidevice scaling. Earth and space.title: The Multiphase Circumgalactic Medium of DESI Emission-line Galaxies at z ∼ 1.5
Earth and space.abstract: We study the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) of emission-line galaxies (ELGs) at z ∼ 1.5, traced by Mg II λ 2796, λ 2803 and C IV λ 1548, λ 1550 absorption lines, using approximately 8000 ELG-quasar pairs from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. Our results show that both the mean rest equivalent width ( W 0 ) profiles and covering fractions of Mg II and C IV increase with ELG stellar mass at similar impact parameters, but show similar distributions when normalized by the virial radius. Moreover, warm C IV gas has a more extended distribution than cool Mg II gas. The dispersion of Mg II and C IV gas velocity offsets relative to the galaxy redshifts rises from ∼100 km s −1 within halos to ∼200 km s −1 beyond. We explore the relationships between Mg II and C IV W 0 and show that the two are not tightly coupled: at a fixed absorption strength of one species, the other varies…

Earth and space.title: Dwarf Galaxy Halo Masses from Spectroscopic and Photometric Lensing in DESI and DES
Earth and space.abstract: We present the most precise and lowest-mass weak lensing measurements of dwarf galaxies to date, enabled by spectroscopic lenses from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and photometric lenses from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) calibrated with DESI redshifts. Using DESI spectroscopy from the first data release, we construct clean samples of galaxies with median stellar masses log 10 ( M * / M ⊙ ) =8.310.1 and measure their weak lensing signals with sources from DES, KiDS, and SDSS, achieving detections with signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) up to 12 for dwarf galaxies ( log 10 ( M * / M ⊙ ) < 9.25)—opening up a new regime for lensing measurements of low-mass systems. Leveraging DES photometry calibrated with DESI, we extend to a photometric dwarf sample of over 700,000 galaxies, enabling robust lensing detections of dwarf galaxies with combined S/N = 30 and a significant…

Earth and space.title: Shock Breakout from Mildly Relativistic Ejecta in a Dense Wind: The Case of EP260321a/SN 2026gzf
Earth and space.abstract: We present shock breakout (SBO) modeling of the recently discovered X-ray transient EP260321a detected by the Einstein Probe mission. Our semianalytic model, based on our previous work, follows the interaction between a supernova ejecta with a mildly relativistic outer envelope and a dense, wind-like circumstellar medium (CSM) by using a thin-shell approximation that incorporates relativistic effects. We find that the observed properties of the X-ray emission are well explained by the breakout emission powered by a high-velocity envelope with a kinetic energy of ∼3.5 × 10 49 erg (excluding the supernova ejecta) and a dense wind characterized by a mass-loss rate of M ̇ ≃ 1.2 × 1 0 − 3 ( v w / 1 0 3 km s − 1 ) M ⊙ yr − 1 , where v w is the wind velocity. The observed burst duration requires the dense CSM to extend up to ∼350 R ⊙ , corresponding to a CSM mass of ∼10 −5 M ⊙ . These results…

Earth and space.title: The Deep Newtonian Regime in Late-time Blast Waves: Inevitable Transition and Distinct Flux Signatures
Earth and space.abstract: In many astrophysical transients, outflows drive shocks into the ambient medium, accelerating electrons to nonthermal energy distributions that produce broadband synchrotron emission. At late times, even initially collimated relativistic jets evolve into quasi-spherical Newtonian blast waves. As the shock decelerates, the post-shock internal energy per particle decreases; below a critical velocity β DN ≈ 0.2 , only a fraction ξ e < 1 of electrons are accelerated to relativistic energies, defining the deep Newtonian (DN) regime. We develop a unified analytic framework for synchrotron emission in this phase, applicable to both single-velocity and stratified ejecta. For gamma-ray burst afterglows in a uniform medium, the DN transition occurs at t DN ≈ 3.7 E 51 1 / 3 n 0 − 1 / 3 yr, yielding a shallower decay by δα = 6( p − 2)/5 relative to standard Newtonian predictions. Earth and space.title: ATLAS. III. Dust around Little Red Dots: Hydrogen Line Ratios beyond Dust-free Non-Case B Models
Earth and space.abstract: We investigate broad hydrogen line ratios in little red dots (LRDs) using five high-redshift ( z > 2) sources from James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) medium/high-resolution spectra in the DAWN JWST Archive (DJA) and 15 low-redshift sources ( z = 0.1–0.9) from the literature, all with broad H β detected at >5 σ . After carefully measuring the broad-line fluxes while accounting for absorption features and neighboring emission lines, we find that the broad H α /H β ratios are very high, ranging from 6 to 30, well above the Case B recombination value. Using plane-parallel C loudy photoionization models with the total line emission from both sides of the slab, we investigate the physical origin of the broad hydrogen line ratios beyond Case B, jointly modeling the Balmer and Paschen line ratios for the subset of one high- z and two low- z LRDs with…

Earth and space.title: Unveiling Multimessenger Emission from Hidden Cores of Microquasars
Earth and space.abstract: Microquasars are radio-emitting X-ray binaries with relativistic jets and are established sources of ∼100 TeV gamma rays, making them promising candidates for cosmic-ray acceleration. Motivated by recent detections of ∼100 TeV photons from Cygnus X-1 and multi-PeV photons from Cygnus X-3, we employ the Astrophysical Multimessenger Emission Simulator (AMES) to model their multimessenger emission from radio to ultrahigh-energy gamma rays. Our modeling suggests that particle acceleration is extremely efficient in the jet region. The observed ≳0.1 PeV gamma rays can originate from either pγ or pp interactions, depending on the location and physical conditions of the emission region, while also reproducing the lower-energy spectra. Earth and space.title: The JADES Mass–Metallicity and Fundamental Metallicity Relations at z ≳ 2 Using New High-redshift Metallicity Calibrations
Earth and space.abstract: We present measurements of the mass–metallicity relation (MZR) and fundamental metallicity relation (FMR) at 1.4 < z < 7.0 using stacked JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 601 star-forming galaxies from the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES). Using the most up-to-date strong-line metallicity calibrations based on high-redshift galaxies, we derive gas-phase metallicities from composite spectra binned by stellar mass, redshift, and star-forming main sequence (SFMS) offset. We find that the MZR slope evolves weakly from z ∼ 0 out to ∼5, with γ ∼ 0.21 ± 0.03, while the normalization decreases smoothly with redshift at a rate of d log ( O / H ) / d z ∼ − 0.1 out to z ∼ 4. Beyond z ≳ 5, the low-mass end continues to decline in metallicity while the high-mass end remains broadly consistent with lower-redshift relations, producing a steeper overall MZR. We additionally find evidence for a…

Earth and space.title: Constraining Galaxy Cluster Triaxiality via Weak Lensing. I. Preparation for the Rubin Data beyond Leading Order
Earth and space.abstract: The 3D mass distributions of galaxy clusters are generally triaxial, a geometry that is difficult to constrain from projected observations. In this work, we measure the projected halo shapes of clusters from weak-lensing (WL) signatures using the Cluster Lensing Mass Modeling software, a tool developed by the Dark Energy Science Collaboration to analyze data from NSF-DOE Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We measure ensemble halo ellipticity on the plane of the sky via axis-aligned stacking and multipole expansion of WL signatures. We study a precursor dataset: the redMaPPer cluster catalog, the metacalibration shape catalog, and the Directional Neighborhood Fitting photometric redshift catalog from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 public data release. We select clusters that have a high centering probability (>90%) of the identified central galaxy, and use the…

Earth and space.title: ID-MAGE. II. The Star-forming Satellites of Low-mass Hosts
Earth and space.abstract: We present the first results of the ongoing Identifying Dwarfs of Magellanic Cloud Analog GalaxiEs (ID-MAGE) survey. This includes new velocities of 78 satellite candidates identified around 35 nearby LMC- and SMC-mass hosts ( D = 4–10 Mpc). Using new Green Bank Telescope H i observations, new optical long-slit spectroscopy from SALT and MDM 2.4 m, and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument DR1, we find six are velocity-confirmed satellite galaxies (6.5 × 10 5 ≤ M ⋆ / M ⊙ ≤ 1.5 × 10 7 ) and 72 are background galaxies. Our results underscore the ability of spectroscopic follow-up to effectively separate satellites from background galaxies. Including the six newly velocity-confirmed satellites and the 19 satellites confirmed in the literature, the ID-MAGE hosts have a combined total of 25 confirmed satellites. This confirmed satellite sample includes the complete satellite populations of…

Earth and space.title: SuperSNEC: Fast and Accurate Light-curve Production for Large Hydrodynamic Model Grids Using Adaptive Gridding
Earth and space.abstract: We present SuperSNEC, an accelerated version of the SuperNova Explosion Code (SNEC) designed for rapid production of large radiation-hydrodynamic model grids using low-zone-count simulations (∼100 zones). The main advance is adaptive gridding of the computational grid, which preserves light-curve fidelity relative to a high-resolution SNEC baseline (∼1000 zones) while delivering a runtime improvement of ∼420 × . SuperSNEC also includes solver optimizations, optimized radioactive-energy deposition and ray-tracing, and improved 56 Ni mixing controls. We quantify the speed-accuracy trade-off for a 100-zone configuration against a 1000-zone reference and define baseline settings for efficient large-grid inference of stripped-envelope supernovae. Our optimized 100-zone setup achieves an rms light-curve residual of 0.022 mag relative to the 1000-zone reference, at a runtime of < 2 s per…

Earth and space.title: Environmental Dependence of Galaxy Properties in the Southern GAMA Regions
Earth and space.abstract: Using data from the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, we investigate how galaxy properties correlate with the local environment, focusing on its two southern regions (G02 and G23) that have not previously been examined in this context. We employ two-point and marked correlation functions to quantify the environmental dependence of galaxy color, stellar mass, luminosity across the u , g , r , J , and K bands, as well as star formation rate (SFR) and specific star formation rate (sSFR). Our results show that u − r and g − r colors are most strongly correlated with local overdensity, followed by stellar mass. The SFR and sSFR exhibit a clear inverse relationship with environmental density, consistent with the trend observed for u -band luminosity, which traces young stellar populations. The galaxies brighter in the g , J , and K bands preferentially inhabit denser regions. We…

Cross-domain.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
Cross-domain.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies…

Cross-domain.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
Cross-domain.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside…

Cross-domain.title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
Cross-domain.abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T 2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime,…

Cross-domain.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
Cross-domain.abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment 1–8 , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear 9–13 . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is…

Cross-domain.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
Cross-domain.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

Cross-domain.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
Cross-domain.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

Cross-domain.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
Cross-domain.abstract: Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers 1,2 . However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples 3 , collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early…

Cross-domain.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
Cross-domain.abstract: Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation 1–9 . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I + –Nuc halogen bonds.…

Cross-domain.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
Cross-domain.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden…

Cross-domain.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
Cross-domain.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD 1–3 . Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge 4 . Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals 5 , and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts 6,7 ; however, the biological basis of this ‘female protective effect’ (FPE) has remained unknown 8,9 . Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that…

Cross-domain.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
Cross-domain.abstract: The ability to observe the social behaviour of others and use observed information to bias future action is a fundamental building block of social cognition1–3. Aggression observation activates hypothalamic neurons relevant for aggression control4,5, but whether observation and experience engage common circuit mechanisms that promote a new shared behavioural policy is unclear. Here we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type-specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behaviour generation and learning. We record longitudinally while animals train through direct aggression experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behaviour and neural activity in a novel aggression context. After training, we detect unique signatures of a shared adaptive behavioural strategy that is absent in animals without training. During aggression observation, observed…

Cross-domain.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
Cross-domain.abstract: RNA language models have achieved strong performances across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by its hierarchical structure, making the integration of structural information into pre-training essential. Existing methods often depend on noisy structural annotations or introduce task-specific biases, limiting model generalizability. Here, we introduce structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model that is pre-trained on millions of RNA sequences and secondary structures data by integrating base pairing interactions into masked language modeling through a novel pair matching operation. The structure-guided mask and nucleotide-level mask are further balanced by a dynamic masking ratio. structRFM learns joint knowledge of sequential and structural data, producing versatile representations, including…

Cross-domain.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
Cross-domain.abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour 1–5 . However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Cross-domain.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
Cross-domain.abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 bp (calibrated years before present or 1950 ce ) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Cross-domain.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
Cross-domain.abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm 1,2 . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated 3–13 . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Biology.title: Deploying liquid intelligence in cancer: Finding answers in our blood
Biology.abstract: Liquid biopsies are one of the few noninvasive procedures for probing disease at the molecular level. They represent a scalable solution to cancer detection and monitoring by capturing tumor-derived signals from circulating biomolecules such as proteins, DNA, RNA, and metabolites. However, these signals are often sparse, heterogeneous, and shaped by genetics, demographics, and comorbidities. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, especially with multimodal foundation models, have proven capable of extracting signals from noisy, high-dimensional data. Pretraining on large cohorts and integrating complementary modalities may improve sensitivity for tumor signals in blood, though significant clinical and infrastructural barriers remain. Biology.title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are conserved brain regions essential for motor control, learning, emotion, and cognition and are implicated in neurological and psychiatric disease, yet a unified cross-species taxonomy of BG cell types is lacking. We present a multiomic consensus atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from humans, macaques, and marmosets spanning eight BG structures, integrating gene expression, open chromatin, and spatial profiling. Alignment across species and to mouse and human whole-brain atlases identifies 61 homologous cell types conserved over 76 million years. Dorsal-ventral spatial identity is more conserved than D1/D2 receptor or striosome/matrix identity, and striatum (STR) D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neurons have distinct molecular, electrophysiological, and morphological features. Biology.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Biology.title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: The basal ganglia are central to motor control, learning, emotion, and reward processing, and their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. Here, we generated a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical human donors. This atlas resolved cell-type- and region-specific landscapes of active and repressive candidate cis -regulatory elements and delineated gene regulatory networks underlying cell identity. We found that the combinatorial expression of homeobox transcription factors provides distinctive molecular descriptors of neuronal cell identities in the basal ganglia. Integration with matched MERFISH spatial transcriptomics further uncovered regional heterogeneity in epigenomic and transcriptional programs. Biology.title: Multiscale spatial atlas of human basal ganglia cell types and communities
Biology.abstract: The human basal ganglia comprise functionally varied nuclei, but their cell-type composition and spatial organization have not been comprehensively resolved. We generated a multi-region, subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas by integrating multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)+ and spatiotemporal enhanced-resolution omics sequencing (Stereo-seq) across four neurotypical donors. Biology.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism
Biology.abstract: Understanding how industrialization reshapes the human metaorganism requires integrating microbiome ecology with host physiology across globally diverse populations. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, immunoglobulin A (IgA) sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Biology.title: Single-cell multimodal atlas reveals regulatory programs in the human brain
Biology.abstract: Direct measurement of chromatin states together with transcription is essential for understanding how cell-type-specific regulatory programs are established and maintained in the adult human brain. Here, we present a large-scale single-cell multimodal atlas by jointly profiling the transcriptome with active (H3K27ac) or repressive (H3K27me3) histone modifications across 18 adult brain regions. We targeted over 750,000 nuclei spanning 160 cell types and integrated these data with chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, 3D genome architecture, and spatial transcriptomes. This framework resolved chromatin states for over 500,000 candidate regulatory elements, identified enhancer-gene links and regulatory programs, revealed Polycomb-associated ultra-long-range contacts, and uncovered brainwide epigenomic heterogeneity. Biology.title: Mesoscale molecular architecture of the striatum across cell types and adult aging
Biology.abstract: The human striatum governs diverse motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors yet lacks the obvious cytoarchitectural boundaries defining functional territories elsewhere in the brain. Using Slide-tags single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics, we profiled 1.1 million cells across 19 postmortem donors to uncover the striatum's spatial organization. These data revealed a consistent subdivision of the striatum into six zones, each defined by molecularly distinct populations of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) and featuring spatially coordinated neuron-astrocyte interaction networks. To determine their structural relevance, we generated a companion mouse spatial atlas that identified four homologous zones that aligned with territories defined by brain-wide afferent projections. Biology.title: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient
Biology.abstract: Whether human-associated environments drive adaptive genome evolution in gut commensal bacteria remains largely unknown. Here, we investigate how genomic adaptation in gut bacteria differs between industrialized and non-industrialized human populations. We generated a collection of isolate genomes spanning diverse host geographies, lifestyles, species, and strains. We first found that, compared with metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), paired isolate genomes recover more functional elements and signals of horizontal gene transfer (HGT). Leveraging isolate genomes from multiple species, we find that strains from industrialized hosts experience an expansion of proteome size and harbor greater pangenome fluidity, driven by recent HGT events. Biology.title: A single-cell and spatial 3D multi-omic atlas of developing human basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: Human basal ganglia (BG) neurons and inhibitory interneurons originate in the ganglionic eminences (GEs), transient structures in the ventral prenatal brain. This study delineates the specification and maturation of GEs and GE-derived neurons using single-nucleus methyl-3C sequencing (snm3C-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and single-molecule chromatin + RNA imaging, and we found heterogeneous temporal progression across GE subregions. Spiny projection neurons (SPNs), the principal cells of the BG, acquire distinct subtypes through synchronized 3D-epigenomic remodeling, in contrast to the asynchronous maturation of other neuron types. Biology.title: Morphoelectric diversity and specialization of primate striatal neuron types
Biology.abstract: The basal ganglia are evolutionarily ancient subcortical nuclei that form interconnected loops with the neocortex and limbic system to regulate movement, learning, habit formation, emotion, and motivation. Their dysfunction contributes to major neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet most cellular-level insights derive from rodent studies, leaving knowledge gaps in humans and translationally relevant primate species. To address this, we generated multimodal Patch-seq data linking transcriptomic identity with morphological and electrophysiological properties in the macaque striatum-the input nucleus of the basal ganglia. We found underappreciated diversity among spiny projection neurons (SPNs), including non-canonical types, and variation aligned with functional gradients. Biology.title: Harmonized brain ontology and 3D atlases for human, macaque, and marmoset basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: A major goal of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is to create a suite of foundational reference cell atlases and associated standards for human and nonhuman primate brains. Central to this goal is the creation of cross-species-harmonized cellular taxonomies and structural parcellations with formal ontologies that can be mapped onto 3D reference frameworks, bridging neuroimaging and cellular and histological resolutions. We describe an iterative approach, focused initially on the basal ganglia, to co-create structural and cellular ontologies for human, macaque, and marmoset brains and to map and refine structural parcellations into neuroimaging-based common coordinate frameworks. Biology.title: Spatial and regulatory organization of cell identity across the primate subcortex
Biology.abstract: Mammalian brain cell identity is shaped by intrinsic factors and external context. We present a spatially resolved transcriptomic and gene regulatory atlas of cell types across all subcortical regions in a primate, the common marmoset. Dense sampling and cross-species integration revealed spatially precise neuronal assemblies, including ones in complex midbrain and diencephalic structures. Chromatin accessibility and transcriptional identity are spatially tuned within and across subcortical structures; spatial gradients within hippocampal subfields are orchestrated by graded transcription factors acting through graded enhancers. Biology.title: Common variation of cell abundances and gene expression in the human striatum
Biology.abstract: The cellular and molecular bases of inter-individual variation in the human brain are not yet understood, particularly beyond the neocortex. Here, we describe cellular and gene-expression variation in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis of 3.9 million nuclei from 178 adult brain donors. People with more astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) in any one brain region tended to have this property in all gray-matter regions sampled. OPC proportions declined by 40% across ages 30-80 in the cortex and striatum. Age-associated gene-expression changes differed substantially across cell types. Biology.title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia
Biology.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet cell-type-resolved epigenomic and 3D genome maps of the human BG remain limited. Here, we present a multimodal single-cell atlas of DNA methylation (261,331 nuclei) and 3D chromatin conformation (229,286 nuclei) from eight subregions, harmonized under the BG consensus taxonomy and integrated with matched data across multiple regulatory layers. We identify millions of differentially methylated regions across cell types, enriched for distinct transcription factor motifs, and link them to disease-associated heritability. We characterize the POU6F2 + STR D2 SMYD2-HTR7 spiny projection neuron (SPN) subtype, with concordant signatures across multiple modalities, and reveal region-specific methylation and contact gradients. Medicine.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
Medicine.abstract: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Medicine.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke — New Directions
Medicine.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

Medicine.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
Medicine.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. Medicine.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis
Medicine.abstract: BACKGROUND: messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. Medicine.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
Medicine.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited. METHODS: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group).
